episode.title: exec JSON events collapse web_search page opens into `other` and drop `results`
episode.before: In the parent state, the v2 app-server Rust protocol already represented `ThreadItem::WebSearch.action` with a v2 `WebSearchAction` enum configured for camelCase serialization. However, the generated v2 TypeScript `ThreadItem` imported `WebSearchAction` from the root generated type set rather than from the v2 type set. That root contract described the older snake_case `open_page` and `find_in_page` discriminators with optional fields, while the v2 producer emitted camelCase `openPage` and `findInPage` values with nullable fields. The generated client contract therefore did not match the observable v2 payload shape, allowing page-open actions to be treated as an unknown/`other` shape and associated action data to be lost.
episode.after: The v2 Rust `WebSearchAction` enum is explicitly exported into the v2 generated type set. Regenerated v2 TypeScript now contains a local `WebSearchAction` union with `search`, `openPage`, `findInPage`, and `other` variants and nullable action fields. The generated v2 `ThreadItem` imports that local definition, and the v2 index re-exports it. The existing core-to-v2 action conversion and app-server event delivery remain unchanged, so clients receive a version-consistent contract for streamed web-search actions.
episode.diff: The implementation adds `#[ts(export_to = "v2/")]` to the Rust v2 `WebSearchAction` enum; generates `schema/typescript/v2/WebSearchAction.ts`; changes generated v2 `ThreadItem.ts` from importing `../WebSearchAction` to importing `./WebSearchAction`; and adds the type to `schema/typescript/v2/index.ts`. The runtime conversion from core web-search actions to v2 `ThreadItem` values was not modified. The commit changes four files with eight insertions and one deletion.

evidence_units.claim: The issue bundle anchors issue 45773 to the pinned implementation ref, identifies the parent commit, and classifies the episode as `observable-validation-and-diagnostics`; it provides the issue title but no issue body, comments, timeline, or linked pull request.

The pinned commit is a single-parent implementation commit titled `fix WebSearchAction type clash between v1 and v2 (#10408)`. Its body states that app-server generated types were still using the v1 snake_case `WebSearchAction`, causing a mismatch with camelCase emitted types, and reports running `just write-app-server-schema`.

The commit changes exactly four app-server protocol artifacts: generated v2 `ThreadItem.ts`, new generated v2 `WebSearchAction.ts`, generated v2 `index.ts`, and Rust `protocol/v2.rs`; the diff is eight insertions and one deletion.

The root protocol model defines `WebSearchAction` with `serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")`, including `open_page` and `find_in_page` wire discriminators; its optional fields are marked for optional TypeScript emission.

The v2 app-server protocol defines a separate `WebSearchAction` enum with `serde` and `ts` tagged camelCase representations. In the after state it has `#[ts(export_to = "v2/")]` and includes `Search`, `OpenPage`, `FindInPage`, and `Other` variants with optional Rust fields.

Before the fix, generated v2 `ThreadItem.ts` imported `WebSearchAction` from `../WebSearchAction`, which resolved to the root type set. After the fix, the import is `./WebSearchAction`, resolving to the v2-local generated type.
evidence_units.source: git show parent and pinned ref for codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/v2/ThreadItem.ts

evidence_units.claim: The root generated TypeScript `WebSearchAction` uses `open_page` and `find_in_page` with optional properties, while the after-state v2 generated type uses `openPage` and `findInPage` with nullable properties. The latter matches the v2 Rust enum's camelCase `ts` attributes and `Option` field representation.
The after-state v2 generated index re-exports `WebSearchAction` from `./WebSearchAction`, making the corrected version-specific contract available from the v2 public type surface.
evidence_units.source: codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/v2/index.ts at the pinned checkout; corresponding commit diff

evidence_units.claim: The v2 `ThreadItem::WebSearch` variant has an `action: Option<WebSearchAction>` field, so its generated TypeScript dependency must resolve to the v2 action definition rather than the root definition.

The existing Rust conversion maps core `WebSearchAction` variants one-for-one into the app-server v2 enum, and `CoreTurnItem::WebSearch` constructs a `ThreadItem::WebSearch` with `Some(WebSearchAction::from(search.action))`; the pinned commit leaves this runtime mapping unchanged.

The app-server event handler converts core `ItemStarted` and `ItemCompleted` items into v2 `ThreadItem` values and sends them through the corresponding server notifications, making the v2 generated `ThreadItem` contract observable to clients.

The protocol crate has an existing `core_turn_item_into_thread_item_converts_supported_variants` test that constructs a core `WebSearchItem` with a Search action and asserts the converted v2 `ThreadItem` contains the expected populated action and fields.

The schema fixture integration test regenerates all TypeScript and JSON artifacts in a temporary directory, compares generated and checked-in file sets and normalized contents, and instructs maintainers to run `just write-app-server-schema` when they differ.

The schema-generation implementation creates root and v2 TypeScript directories from Rust `ts-rs` derives and generates per-directory index files; the repository exposes this through the `write-app-server-schema` just target named in the commit validation note.
evidence_units.source: codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/export.rs:88-137 and justfile:72-73 at the pinned checkout

evidence_units.claim: The checked-in v2 JSON schema describes `openPage` and `findInPage` discriminators and nullable URL/pattern fields, corroborating that the intended v2 wire contract is camelCase and nullable even though the commit's changed generated artifacts are TypeScript files.

candidate_atomics.name: align_v2_web_search_action_schema_binding
candidate_atomics.description: Make the generated v2 client contract for web-search actions version-specific and bind `ThreadItem.action` to it, so the client-facing representation matches the v2 producer instead of the root/v1 representation.

semantic_action.intent: Make v2 web-search action payloads parseable and observable with the same discriminator and nullability contract used by the v2 producer, preventing page-open actions from falling through to an incompatible unknown/`other` interpretation.
semantic_action.module_role: versioned app-server protocol schema generation and aggregate-type binding
semantic_action.pre_state: The v2 Rust `WebSearchAction` was already used by `ThreadItem`, but it was not exported into the v2 generated type set. Generated v2 `ThreadItem` consequently resolved the same-named type to the root snake_case contract with `open_page`/`find_in_page` and optional fields.
semantic_action.post_state: A v2-local generated `WebSearchAction` union exists with camelCase `openPage`/`findInPage` discriminators and nullable action fields, `ThreadItem.action` imports it locally, and the v2 index exposes it.
semantic_action.validation: The generated v2 artifact, local ThreadItem import, and v2 index export are checked by schema fixture regeneration/comparison; the existing Rust conversion test verifies that the runtime ThreadItem contains a populated WebSearchAction before serialization.

candidate_workflows.name: repair_versioned_generated_protocol_contract
candidate_workflows.description: Correct a generated client contract when a shared type name resolves to the wrong protocol version, then validate the regenerated artifact set while preserving the existing runtime conversion path.

workflow_graph.goal: Allow v2 clients to recognize streamed web-search action variants and retain their typed action fields in `ThreadItem` events.
workflow_graph.entry_state: Core web-search events already become v2 ThreadItem values, but generated v2 TypeScript points `ThreadItem.action` at the incompatible root snake_case `WebSearchAction` contract and no v2 action artifact exists.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The v2 generated contract points `ThreadItem.action` at a local camelCase/nullable `WebSearchAction` union, the v2 public index exposes that type, and generated fixtures agree with the Rust protocol definitions.
unresolved_or_deferred: The existing protocol unit test covers core-to-v2 Search conversion, not an end-to-end TypeScript parse of `openPage` or `findInPage`.

The issue title mentions dropped `results`, but the changed WebSearchAction definitions contain no `results` field; the checkout establishes the discriminator/type mismatch but not the exact downstream result-dropping implementation.
The runtime conversion and notification plumbing were already present and were intentionally left unchanged; the fix is at the generated versioned contract boundary.

unresolved_questions: The issue bundle has no body, comments, timeline, author/review discussion, or linked pull request. The failure mechanism is therefore grounded in the concrete before/after schema mismatch and the implementation commit message rather than issue discussion.

The bundle title refers to exec JSON events and dropped `results`, but the pinned diff only changes app-server v1/v2 generated type binding. No direct `results` field or downstream exec JSON consumer appears in the inspected changed files, so the exact result-loss path remains unresolved.
No explicit regression test for a TypeScript consumer parsing an `openPage` or `findInPage` payload was added by the pinned commit.

The pinned commit subject references PR `#10408` while the bundle anchors issue `45773`; the bundle identifies the pinned ref as the resolution, but the available metadata does not independently explain that numbering relationship.

The targeted Rust test was not executed during extraction because `cargo` was unavailable in the environment; the validation record relies on the checked-in test source, fixture oracle, generated artifacts, and the commit's stated schema-generation run.
